brief: Wilson's running thesis (clearing hyperscaler-earnings and midterm event risk enables a year-end rally led by mega-caps; the AI sentiment pendulum swung too far since end-Q2, so opportunities are re-emerging) has been bruised over the past two weeks. He argues this week's underlying data is still positive: hyperscaler cloud growth is accelerating, financing visibility improved via Meta's equity raise and Oracle's brought-forward breakeven guidance, and cyber risk is in a bull market after the Binance hack. Yet Nasdaq fell over 3.5% on Intel, software and Alphabet/Amazon core-business concerns, a gap he reads as the market not yet listening. Positioning has broken down: the AI-winners-vs-AI-at-risk trade and Mag7 outperformance trend have failed, correlations are unusually dislocated, and the S&P ex-AI and European equities are outperforming US tech. He sees no sign of AI demand slowing, calls the 2007/08 financing-crisis comparison misplaced versus a 1990s cycle framing, cites Microsoft and Amazon management commentary on usage and ROIC confidence, and concludes capex growth may have paused toward efficiency while reports of an AI capex "demise" are exaggerated.
